value.a: Three load-bearing assumptions, each measured 2026-09-07. (1) Folding collides no two system words: every verb table, view table, learning_block SIGNALS, ground_loop COMMANDS, ruling verbs, skill_block verbs, and every ~/.cairn/devices/*/0/bin/ directory is lowercase-unique. (2) No keyword slot is also a free-text slot: learning_block's `<signal> <words>` vs `<target> <words>` is disambiguated by SIGNALS membership, so folding the membership test and not the stored words keeps his words verbatim; `cairn review <id> "words"` folds only the id prefix. (3) Both ruling matchers read only his text: `ruled_marks` reads the_ruling_verbatim and the hook scans transcript user messages (cli.py:213-217); CC's prose never reaches either.

(a) argparse in the tester CLI is case-sensitive and cannot fold; the build folds argv tokens that start with '-' before parse_args and leaves target paths alone. (b) The bash sites cannot import the python primitive; they fold with `${var,,}` and the proof drives them as subprocesses. Status words typed by him have no live seam today (no CLI takes a stage token), so `clearance.clear` and transitions' target doors fold their target upward as a forward guard; a future CLI that takes a stage word inherits it.
As carried in the falsifier field: nine behavioural teeth over the live entry points plus two wrong-intent teeth (free text verbatim; stored workflow strings untouched). Horizon: this session.

One real collision, settled by the ruling. ruling.py:138 ('UPPERCASE, WORD-BOUNDED, DELIBERATE') and test_ruling.py:286-311 encode that lowercase 'ruled' must NOT confirm.
